title: First Principles Triage and Runbook Ops Playbook
author: Aisha Thompson
body:
Summary:
This playbook codifies a first-principles approach to triage, containment, restoration, and post-incident evidence capture for Redwood's serving and orchestration systems. It standardizes decision-making heuristics (not rote checklists) so responders can make consistent, auditable choices during high-uncertainty incidents.

Intended audience:
- Primary: first responders, on-call engineers, SRE rotation leads
- Secondary: incident commanders, support leads, product liaisons

Scope:
- Applies to production-hosted and dedicated Redwood inference endpoints, routing/control plane, autoscaler, and KV-cache services.
- Excludes: developer sandboxes, local dev workflows, and customer-managed private control planes (see reference runbooks in eng-private-deployments).

Goals and non-goals:
- Goals:
  - Restore meaningful customer traffic within SLO-defined windows (see SLOs section).
  - Preserve forensic evidence for regulatory & billing audits.
  - Make triage decisions that minimize blast radius and enable progressive escalation/fallback.
- Non-goals:
  - Exhaustive troubleshooting of non-production issues.
  - Replacing service-specific runbooks (this is a guiding framework that links to those runbooks).

Severity classification (quick reference):
1) Sev0 / Major outage: >50% of customer requests failing or systemic data corruption; requires bridge within 15 minutes.
2) Sev1 / Major degradation: latency SLOs breached for >10% of tokens or persistent error-rate spike >5% for 15+ minutes.
3) Sev2 / Partial: isolated region/tenant impact; elevated errors for a single model or capacity pool.
4) Sev3 / Informational: low-impact regression, non-urgent customer report.

SLOs and restoration windows (example):
- Token-latency p95: 300ms target, SLO window: 30d; breach defined as p95 > 400ms for >1h with customer impact.
- Availability: 99.95% monthly.
- Restoration windows: Sev0 — bridge and public status within 15 min, functional recovery target 2h; Sev1 — alert & triage within 30 min, recovery target 6h; Sev2 — triage within 2h, recovery 24h.

Decision heuristics (first principles):
1) Protect evidence: if incident may affect billing/integrity, snapshot logs/KV-store and capture crashdumps before mass restarts.
2) Minimize user blast radius: favor traffic-shaping, rate-limits, or routing to degraded-but-safe model variants over full service shutdown.
3) Prefer reversible changes: configuration toggles and rate limits over irreversible migrations.
4) Escalate early: if triage confidence < 60% after 30 minutes at Sev0/Sev1, call an Incident Commander.

Roles and responsibilities (one-line):
- First Responder: acknowledge alert, collect evidence, make safe containment moves.
- Incident Commander (IC): coordinate cross-functional response, customer messaging, and retrospective ownership.
- Service Owner: domain SME, implements and validates fixes.
- SRE Lead: approves large-scale rollbacks and capacity changes.
- Communications Lead: drafts public and customer templates.

Runbook anchor procedure: initial 18-minute triage (used as a mental model)
1) 0:00–0:02 — Acknowledge, set bridge channel, post short status: severity estimate, likely impacted services, initial mitigation (if any).
   - Slack template: "[ACK] Sev{n} — {service} — initial triage in progress. Bridge: {link}."
2) 0:02–0:06 — Evidence capture: collect latest logs (last 30 minutes), snapshot KV-cache metadata, export controller metrics, and note any recent deploys/rollouts.
   - CLI snippets:
     ```bash
     # capture last 30m logs for service
     rbctl logs service/my-service --since 30m > /tmp/my-service-logs.txt
     # snapshot kv cache metadata
     rbctl kv snapshot --service my-model-pool --out /tmp/kv-snap.json
     ```
3) 0:06–0:12 — Rapid hypothesis generation: enumerate top 3 root causes (capacity, recent deploy, upstream network, data corruption).
4) 0:12–0:18 — Containment action 1: implement the least disruptive mitigation from the hypothesis list (example: switch traffic to warm pool, apply per-tenant rate-limits, disable caching layer write-behavior). Record the exact command and operator.
5) Post-18: If restored, proceed to evidence hardening and RCA. If not, escalate to IC.

Containment play examples (choose lowest-privilege/reversible):
- Re-route traffic to compatible model variants (CLI):
  ```bash
  rbctl traffic update --route /v1/generate --to model:llama-2-13b-quant --weight 100
  ```
- Apply a per-tenant throttle for noisy tenants:
  ```bash
  rbctl quota set --tenant tenant-123 --requests-per-minute 2000
  ```
- Disable aggressive KV writes temporarily:
  ```bash
  rbctl feature disable kv_writeback --service my-cache
  ```

Evidence capture checklist (always capture in order):
- Timestamps and timezone-normalized event windows.
- Full request-id traces for a representative sample (min 5).
- Controller and node-level metrics (CPU, GPU mem, queue length) spanning -60m..+15m around incident start.
- Snapshot of active rollouts and model version pins.
- Any relevant billing/usage spikes.
- Export of error payloads and stack traces.

Escalation matrix (summary):
- If containment not effective after 30m at Sev0/1 -> IC + SRE Lead + Product PM on-call.
- If evidence indicates data integrity risk -> Inform Security and Legal (follow security-and-compliance incident runbook).
- If customer-sensitive data is suspected -> mark confidentiality: restricted and follow chain-of-custody.

On-call rotation and mentorship guidance (unique element):
- Rotation model: two-week primary on-call + four-week secondary; shadow week for new hires before primary.
- Mentorship pairing: every new on-call engineer is paired with a mentor for the first 3 rotations; mentor runs a 60-minute pre-rotation walkthrough covering common runbooks and CLI exercises.
- Post-shift debrief: primary fills a 10-min structured debrief form in the bridge after each shift (what alerts fired, any runbook gaps, triage confidence).

Game day playbook (90-minute template):
- Objective: validate triage heuristics and evidence capture under simulated KV-cache corruption and aggressive autoscaler oscillation.
- Pre-game: schedule with all participating teams, pre-seed synthetic load, and mark customer impact as simulated.
- Scenario timeline:
  - 0–10m: inject synthetic errors at controller and amplify a slow build-up of queue length.
  - 10–25m: expect first-responder to follow initial 18-minute triage; verify evidence artifacts exist.
  - 25–45m: require the IC to authorize a traffic-shift to warm pool and a rollback of the latest model rollout.
  - 45–75m: validate rollback, run a smoke test suite, and confirm metrics restore.
  - 75–90m: structured retro and runbook updates.

Status page & customer comm templates (editable):
- Public status (short):
  "We are investigating elevated request errors affecting text generation in US-East. Impact: intermittent failures for some customers. Mitigation in progress; next update in 30 minutes."

- Incident page (long):
  "Timeline: 10:14 UTC — Elevated 5xx rate observed; 10:20 UTC — bridge stood up; 10:27 UTC — initial containment: traffic routed to warm pool; 11:07 UTC — rollback of model rollout; 11:45 UTC — services stable; 12:00 UTC — full validation completed. Customer impact: intermittent request failures for ~18% of requests between 10:14-11:07 UTC. Root cause: faulty model rollout interacting with KV-cache eviction logic. Next steps: harden rollout gating and add KV eviction anomaly detection."

- Customer email template (concise):
  "Subject: Incident affecting Redwood text-generation in US-East — [Resolved]

  Hi {customer_name},

  We experienced intermittent errors impacting text-generation requests in US-East from {start_time} to {end_time}. We restored service by routing traffic to a warm pool and rolling back a model rollout. Your account saw {approximate_percent}% failed/latency-impacted requests. We will follow up with an RCA and proposed mitigations by {date}. If you require credits or a dedicated call, reply to this message and we will schedule it."

Post-incident workflow (team actions):
1) IC prepares a one-page incident chronicle within 24 hours and shares with stakeholders.
2) Evidence handoff: all captured artifacts uploaded to the incident bucket with checksum and chain-of-custody note.
3) Technical RCA: service owners produce detailed analysis (3–7 business days recommended).
4) Remediation plan: prioritized action items with owners and ETA (target: at least one mitigating fix within 7 days).
5) Follow-up customer communication: scheduled by Customer Success with IC input.

RCA example structure (required fields):
- Summary (one paragraph)
- Impact window and affected tenants
- Root cause analysis with evidence links
- Contributing factors
- Corrective and preventative actions (owner + ETA)
- Lessons learned and runbook updates made

Runbook governance and upkeep:
- Every runbook referenced from this playbook must have an owner and a quarterly review date.
- After every Sev0/1 incident, update the runbook within 10 business days or create a backlog ticket linking to the incident.
- Maintain a runbook change log at the top of each runbook with dates, approver, and short rationale.

Appendix: quick forensic commands and artifact locations
- Export controller metrics: `rbctl metrics export controller --from "-60m" --to "+15m" --out /tmp/controller-metrics.csv`
- Collection bucket: s3://redwood-incidents/incident-{incident_id}/artifacts/ (ensure checksum.md5 is present)
- Evidence retention: default 90 days for standard incidents, 365 days for any incident that may affect billing or legal obligations.

Notes and references:
- Related SOPs: security-and-compliance/incident-response-security, eng-private-deployments/deployment-guides
- See also: postmortem templates (incident-comm-and-postmortem-framework-2026) and on-call mentorship materials in eng-sre/team-wiki.

Revision history:

- 2024-09-10: expanded evidence checklist and CLI snippets (Daniel Cho)
- 2025-11-02: added mentorship pairing and game-day template; clarified SLO restoration windows (Priya Nair)

Contact and escalation list (on-call directory links):
- Primary SRE rotation: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/rotation-directory
- IC on-call schedule: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/ic-schedule

End of playbook.
